images.title: Four kinds of angle
images.purpose: Show that angles are named acute, right, obtuse or straight by comparing with 90° and 180°.
images.composition: One single row of 4 equal panels with wide space between them.
images.exact_structure: One row of exactly 4 angles with a shared base on the right, each in its own equal space: 35° drawn in teal #0072B2, 90° with a square corner mark in amber #E69F00, 120° in teal #0072B2, and 180° as a straight line in amber #E69F00. No other objects.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
an angle drawn with a size very different from its label
images.takeaway: Less than 90° is acute, more is obtuse.
images.description: A row of four angles of 35°, 90°, 120° and 180°, named acute, right, obtuse and straight.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to compare each angle with the square corner and say its name.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture of the angle itself; one clean image carries it.
